notes: §1985:XV.3.2.4 GR16: "If the first execution of the first nondeclarative procedure in the program causes the debugging section to be executed", DEBUG-LINE identifies its first statement, DEBUG-NAME its name and DEBUG-CONTENTS 'START PROGRAM'; anything no rule sets stays spaces (GR11). Since PB5415, EmitDispatcher emits EmitDebugCause(StartProgram) only on an instance's first activation (the __dbgStarted flag), EmitDebugRunner uses the subject's line for that cause and DebugItem.ContentsFor writes START PROGRAM. Since kb/Work PB5568, an empty FIRST section is a procedure with a pc of its own, so it compiles and is the START PROGRAM subject: DS S0 START PROGRAM, then P1 (the section has no first statement, so its DEBUG-LINE is the section header's line, GR12 leaving the identification to the implementor). Probed at 85 (classes b, c, d): paragraph subject F1 in a CALLed program: first CALL [33][F1][START PROGRAM], second CALL spaces, CALL after CANCEL START PROGRAM again (docs/conformance/3/D-DEBUG-PROCEDURE); section subject S1: START PROGRAM once; ALL PROCEDURES: S0 and P0 both START PROGRAM; subject not first: FALL THROUGH; no DEBUGGING MODE: section not run; --std 2002: COBOL0902; empty first section S0: START PROGRAM. Classes a, e, f do not reach a procedure trigger.
